I've been working this land for 25 years. I know Quzhou's soil — sandy loam, alkaline, gets dry in spring before the rains come. My well pump is reliable, so I'm not too worried about drought. Two of my family members work in town now, so I have to be realistic about labor. I can't spend as much time on cotton as I used to.

Here's how I'm thinking through each crop:

**Wheat (5 mu, winter-spring):** This is my anchor crop. I've grown wheat my whole life. I'll plant improved Jimai-series seed — I know it, it does well here, and I can get it from the village supply co-op. I apply base fertilizer before planting and topdress at jointing. Four irrigations: overwintering, jointing, heading, grain-filling. I rotary-till after maize harvest in October, then plant wheat. Two pesticide passes — one herbicide in winter, one for rust and aphids in spring. I expect around 420 kg/mu.

**Maize (5 mu, summer):** Same plot as the wheat, planted right after I harvest wheat in June. I use Zhengdan 958 hybrid — everyone around here uses it and it's proven. I direct-seed without tillage to save time and keep moisture in. Topdress nitrogen at the jointing and tasseling stages. Three irrigations. I expect 550 kg/mu.

**Stevia (4 mu, spring-autumn):** This is my cash crop now. I have a contract with the processing company in town. I use improved rooted cuttings from the company. Stevia likes water but not waterlogging, so I irrigate carefully — about 5 times. I'm not as heavy on nitrogen as I am with grain; too much makes the leaves bitter and lowers glycoside content. I till with a rotary before transplanting in April. Two pesticide applications, mainly for aphids and spider mites.

**Cotton (5 mu, spring-autumn):** I still grow cotton because I know it and the price holds. But it's heavy work — my back isn't what it was, and my son is gone. I plough deep in April before planting hybrid seed. Cotton drinks water and needs potassium, so I make sure to apply more K here than anywhere else. Five irrigations, five pesticide rounds — bollworm pressure is real every year. I expect 240 kg/mu of seed cotton.
